title: Cohort-thresholded prefetch-safe eviction: proof obligations and rollout plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Eviction of KV cache slots during continuous batching + aggressive prefetching has produced correctness regressions and tail-latency spikes for multi-prefix requests. This ticket designs and verifies a cohort-thresholded eviction policy that combines per-prefix cohort counters, TTL decay, and an in-flight prefetch safeguard to provide provable safety properties while preserving GPU memory utilization targets. The goal is a deployable policy with tests, perf guardrails, and a staged rollout.
background: Current behavior: LRU+TTL heuristics evict slots without coordination with active prefetch cohorts, causing invalidated KV reads and repeated prefetch churn under bursty traffic.
Observed problems: repetitive GPU rematerialization, increased per-request token cost, and degraded SLOs for tail latency on multi-prefix pipelines.

Prior art: cohort ideas in ENG-61234 and eviction audits in ENG-47205 inspired per-tenant grouping; this ticket focuses on per-prefix cohorts combined with a deterministic thresholding rule to avoid evicting recently-prefetched slices.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads (link in links).

Formal proof sketch (informal but rigorous) showing eviction rule preserves: no eviction of slots with active in-flight references OR prefetch cohort count above threshold until cohort cooling completes.
Unit + integration tests that reproduce previous regression and show fix (CI green).
Performance regression <=2% p50 token latency, and tail (p99) improvement of at least 10% for observed workloads in benchmark harness.
Memory utilization curve matches target: <1.5x baseline transient overhead during aggressive prefetch bursts; sustained steady-state GPU memory <= configured budget + 5%.
Canary rollout plan documented and automated: canary flag, telemetry checks, auto-rollback thresholds.
design_notes: Eviction policy components: cohort counter (per-prefix), temporal TTL decay, LRU score as tie-breaker, and an 'inflight_hold' guard that marks slots referenced by active batches for eviction immunity until batch completes.
Cohort thresholding: slots with cohort_count >= COHORT_THRESHOLD are not eligible for eviction until cohort_count decays below COOL_DOWN window or explicit eviction signal from allocator.

Prefetch integration: prefetches increment cohort_count; failed prefetches decrement on error path. Continuous batching increments an inflight reference which sets inflight_hold until the batch finishes and the KV consumer acknowledges usage.
Trade-offs: stronger safety increases memory retention; we mitigate with a dynamic COHORT_THRESHOLD tuned per-tenant based on recent hit-rate and allocation pressure metrics.

Fallbacks: if memory pressure exceeds hard limit, policy triggers an emergency demotion (non-atomic) that evicts lowest LRU among non-inflight slots, with panic telemetry and metric flag for rollback.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype in local fuzzer harness + unit tests (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Run workloads in staging with continuous-batching traces and prefetch enabled; tune COHORT_THRESHOLD and COOL_DOWN parameters (1 week).
Phase 3: Canary rollout on 5% traffic with auto-rollback metrics (SLO breach, memory spike) (1 week).
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring and postmortem checklist (1 week).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Cohort counters can be inflated by repeated speculative prefetches -> Mitigation: enforce max_cohort_per_prefix per time window and sample-based decay.
Risk: Inflight_hold leaks if batches crash -> Mitigation: epoched lease with TTL and periodic reconciler to clear orphaned holds.
Risk: Emergency demotions may destabilize SLOs -> Mitigation: restrict emergency demotions to non-critical tenants and require operator approval above threshold.
test_plan: Deterministic replay test that previously caused invalidation, assert no stale reads.
Fuzzbench with mixed TTL/LRU scenarios and simultaneous prefetch bursts for 1M requests.
End-to-end perf run against benchmark corpus (chat + long-context sampling) comparing baseline vs new policy.
